title: Rare disease drug: ₹9 crore a year cut to ₹2.5 lakh

slides.head: Rare disease drug: ₹9 crore a year cut to ₹2.5 lakh
What happened
slides.body: Seven children with AHDS get a free year of tiratricol from Nov 30.

slides.head: Why it matters
slides.body: The commercial drug costs about ₹4.68 crore to ₹9 crore per child a year; the compounded version about ₹2.5 lakh.

slides.head: Did you know
slides.body: One family had to arrange about ₹12-13 lakh for just one month's supply from Germany.

slides.head: What to watch
slides.body: The first batch handover on Nov 30 and whether more families get access. Ask: What stops more rare-disease drugs from being compounded this way?

captions.instagram:
Rare disease drug: ₹9 crore a year cut to ₹2.5 lakh

Seven Indian children with Allan-Herndon-Dudley syndrome will get a year's supply of tiratricol free on Nov 30, after an effort led by Hyderabad paediatrician Dr Sivaranjani Santosh and Access to Medicines India.

Why it matters: The commercial drug costs about ₹4.68 crore to ₹9 crore per child a year; the compounded version about ₹2.5 lakh.

Source: The Hindu. Image: The Hindu
